80210601.text: Over there! It looks like they're sleeping...

80210603.text: "Sleep well, Father. Sleep well, my beloved people."

80210604.text: "When you awake, that which differentiates us shall be no more."

80210101.text: Hey, look at those Hilichurls over there...

80210103.text: Weren't they acting super agitated just a little while ago? Why are they so calm all of a sudden?

80210105.text: ...In the new world, they bade farewell to the shrouded sun.

80210106.text: At last, they no longer needed to dwell on their suffering, or try to differentiate between various thoughts of blasphemy.

80210107.text: Such was the price they paid, and thus their souls became cleansed and pure.

80210301.text: Looks like the same thing is happening over here too. The Hilichurls are calm...

80210303.text: We've reclaimed an endless amount of time to love.

80210304.text: Release your tears. You no longer need to hold back your sorrow.

80210701.text: Grandpa Amadhiah, is everyone alright? The Abyss Order seems to be up to something nearby...

80210702.text: The Abyss Order? This is the first I'm hearing of it...

80210703.text: Thank you for your concern, but as far as I'm aware, it's been business as usual here in the village.

80210705.text: Oh! Also... You didn't happen to come across any clues about the missing villager while we were gone, did you?

80210706.text: Huh? Someone's gone missing, you say? Who would that be?

80210710.text: You know... The young guy from Vimara Village... The one you've been looking for all this time. You posted a commission with the Sumeru Adventurers' Guild...

80210711.text: That's kind of the whole reason we're here, actually... Your missing person's commission.

80210712.text: Ah, I do apologize, you two... I hope I'm not worrying you too much. I'm sure it's just my age making me forgetful again...

80210713.text: At least right now, I can't seem to recall whatever it is you're referring to... Perhaps you should try asking someone else?

80210714.text: But, how is that... *sigh* Alright. Thanks for your help, Grandpa Amadhiah.

80210715.text: Something's definitely not right. We just talked to Grandpa Amadhiah about the missing villager. There's no way he could've forgotten all about him just like that...

80210716.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Could everyone's memories of the missing villager have been erased again?

80210803.text: Um, that guy you said a bunch of nice things about earlier? The one you always used to chat with...

80210804.text: He's around twenty years old... You said he was a kind, warm-hearted sort of person...

80210805.text: Oh! I know who you're talking about...

80210807.text: There aren't many young people who've earned that kind of praise from me. If you're certain that's what I said...

80210808.text: Then, there's only person who fits the bill — no doubt about it... But, why'd you say he's gone missing?

80210811.text: Yeah! I just saw him leave the village. There was someone else with him too. They couldn't have gone far.

80211901.text: Oh, right! That's exactly what Atossa described!

80211902.text: Come to think of it, every time we talked, it always seemed to be around dusk, just like right now.

80211903.text: Time always passed by really slowly. Even when it felt like we'd been talking for hours, the sun would still be at the same position in the sky...

80211904.text: Yep, that has to be it! This is definitely Atossa's memory!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the place Atossa once indicated

80212102.text: Oh... You know me? That's quite the surprise. I don't believe I've met you before...

80212103.text: Ah, I see. It was the memory, wasn't it? Your sibling's memory. You saw... the me from back then.

80212104.text: This is Atossa's memory. I came here to say goodbye to her...

80212105.text: But, I suppose I'll just leave her a message instead. Come, let's find somewhere else to talk...

80212203.text: I suppose you could call it the realm of my consciousness. I'm someone who no longer exists in the real world, after all... as you well know.

80212205.text: Ah, it's nothing. I still have enough strength to play the part of a good host. I've always hoped that I'd get the chance to talk to you like this, and now, the time has finally arrived.

80212206.text: (This is a rare opportunity for me as well. I should try to learn as much information from Caribert as I can.)

80212209.text: Extreme sorrow and pain... Hope and regret coursing through your veins... and a degree of Abyssal power that defies comprehension...

80212210.text: Father told me that once I possessed all those elements, I would become the Loom of Fate.

80212211.text: But, despite his intentions for me, I never truly became the Loom of Fate. I was merely used as a means for its "construction"...

80212212.text: In truth, I died the moment I set everything in motion.

80212213.text: The "person" you see before you now is nothing but a remnant of consciousness leftover within the Loom of Fate.

80212214.text: (Caribert is dead... That's why he no longer exists outside of people's memories.)

80212215.text: As for your question... The Loom of Fate is a device capable of weaving Ley Lines.

80212217.text: In its primitive form, it can only be used to create and implant memories. But, as more of it is completed, its power becomes stronger and stronger... Until finally, it has the power to weave real Ley Lines of its own.

80212218.text: Once fully completed, the moment it gains the power to weave Ley Lines, it loses the lower-level ability to influence memories...

80212219.text: ...But it also becomes a tool that can change the entire world.

80212220.text: So that was the source of your ability to implant memories?

80212221.text: Yes. I have the ability to control the Loom in its semi-completed form. I suppose you could think of it as a form of compensation...

80212222.text: ...After all, its existence cost me my life.

80212223.text: (So the memories that suddenly appeared in Dain's mind were implanted by Caribert through the half-finished Loom of Fate...)

80212224.text: (That makes sense... But, I'm still lost as to why he went so far as to "introduce" himself to all the residents of Vimara Village...)

80210402.text: The chance to just stop and talk like this is certainly not easy to come by... Wouldn't you agree?

80210406.text: The one against Dain, I mean.

80210407.text: I didn't expect that after everything, he would still hesitate to raise his sword against me...

80210408.text: Were it not for that... Perhaps I'd still be no match for the Twilight Sword. Even after five hundred years.

80210501.text: *yawn*... So sleepy. Paimon's head still feels all fuzzy...

80210502.text: Paimon woke up a little earlier than you, so Paimon will fill you in. The villagers said they saw us sleeping near the village yesterday. They couldn't wake us up no matter how hard they tried, so they decided to just bring us back here.

80210503.text: Oh, and Dain came by just now. It looked like he was injured...

80210504.text: He didn't say anything, though. Just made sure that you were alright and left... Kinda seemed like he had a lot on his mind... But, that's Dain for you...

80210507.text: Hmm, let's think for a second. We were in that memory, and we saw that guy you called Caribert...

80210508.text: He was the missing villager we'd been trying to find, right? And after that... Paimon doesn't remember what happened...

80211103.text: Oh, it's you two. I was just about to go looking for you. I wanted to thank you.

80211104.text: I was part of the search party, so I... remember what happened to Caribert now.

80211105.text: Honestly... I just... can't believe I forgot something so important...

80211107.text: He always seemed to appear out of nowhere, and now... he left just as quickly...

80211126.text: If Caribert wants me to forget about the time we spent together, then I'm willing to try.

80211127.text: I relied on him for a lot of things. But, I'm sure with enough time, even the deepest of attachments can fade.

80211128.text: "You must get along with each other, the two of you."

80211109.text: It's funny, but... I have this feeling he told me the same thing. I just can't seem to remember when...

80211110.text: I guess it doesn't really matter, anyway. Life is made up of a series of memories. As long as I hold onto our time together... He'll always be a part of my life.

80211111.text: I'm just happy I got to meet him. So, who cares what happens in the future, right?

80211113.text: Okay, I'll admit, I'm just putting on a brave face.

80211115.text: ...Otherwise, why would he just leave like that without saying goodbye?

80211116.text: I'm sure... he had his reasons.

80211117.text: Hehe, you don't need to comfort me. I'll be okay.

80211118.text: It's just like Caribert said... It's the things we overcome that make life more precious.

80211119.text: And, y'know... If he has a heart, maybe he'll come back and see me one day.

80211120.text: Anyway, thanks for all your hard work, you two. I promised I'd help Granny Jehiet with something, so I should head back. Goodbye!

80211121.text: Well... That should be it, right? Everyone's lives can go back to normal now...

80211122.text: Oh, right! Weren't you about to tell Paimon what happened after your conversation with Caribert?

80211123.text: (Right... What was it that happened...? I can't remember...)

80211124.text: (Huh? It feels like there's something in my pocket...)

80211125.text: Uh. A picture? Where'd that come from? Let Paimon see...

80211701.text: Right! Paimon totally forgot about the Ley Line disturbances. We're in someone else's memory...

80211702.text: Just like how you entered your sibling's memory last time!

80211703.text: That would also explain why we seem to be at a time before he went missing... It's a memory, after all.

80211706.text: Right! If he's someone who only exists in people's memories, then we're finally on the same turf!

80211707.text: But, didn't Bahram just say he saw him leave the village with someone? Where should we go look for him...

80211708.text: Who knows how long this Ley Line disturbance is gonna last... We might not have that much time. And we don't even know whose memory this is...

80211709.text: Let's go through what we know so far...

80211710.text: Good idea! That'll help us narrow things down.

80211711.text: We pretty much figured out that the missing villager has the ability to...

80211712.text: Implant memories into the minds of others.

80211713.text: Right, that! Could we try to figure out a bit more about him using what we know of his ability?

80211714.text: Like, does it maybe leave a trace that would somehow give him away?

80211715.text: (Hmm... Implanting memories into the minds of others must be an imperfect process. There's no way the new memories could perfectly blend in with the old ones. There has to be some kind of tell...)

80210201.text: A missing villager... Did I really forget something so important? As the chief, I can't afford to be so negligent.

80210901.text: Strange... Bahram seems to remember him... And, apparently, he just saw him?

80210902.text: Do you think maybe... It's not that there's something wrong with people's memories, but that we've somehow returned to a time before he went missing?

80210903.text: (I doubt returning to the past would be that simple.)

80210904.text: (Given everything Dain mentioned about disturbances with the Ley Lines, I'd say it's far more likely this is related to memories in some way...)

80210905.text: (I need to think carefully... What's really going on...?)

80211001.text: ...So, you see, Granny Jehiet was a mercenary when she was younger. She just talks like that out of habit. She's not trying to scare the children on purpose, hehe...

80211002.text: Oh, there I go again... always talking about my own things. Do you, maybe, have anything you want to share?

80211003.text: Um... It's okay if you don't. You could also just... Talk about what you think of me?

80211004.text: Oh, I... I think you're an incredibly strong and thoughtful young woman.

80211005.text: You'll meet many amazing people and live a very happy life... You won't miss someone like me...

80211006.text: Huh...? Are those your friends over there?

80211007.text: (We finally found him. But why does he look kind of familiar...?)

80211008.text: Oh, right. This version of Atossa hasn't met us yet...

80211009.text: Friends? I guess you could say that. It must have taken them a lot of effort to find me...

80211010.text: So... I should see what they need. I'm sorry, Atossa. We'll have to continue this conversation another time.

80211011.text: Another time, huh... Um, yeah! Okay! I'll head back to the village, then. Talk to you... some other time!

80211012.text: #It's nice to see you, {NICKNAME}. I believe this is the first time we've met.

80211014.text: (Factoring in the memories, the Abyss Order, the Loom of Fate, and everything else, I need to think of the one person that can connect all of this together...)

80211801.text: No wonder! All this time, and the sky hasn't changed a bit. That must mean... Time isn't passing!

80211802.text: That's the tell of the fake memories!

80211803.text: The implanted memories are basically taking place outside the regular twenty-four hours of the day.

80211804.text: If the memories included the regular passage of time, it would be easy for people to tell that something was off.

80211805.text: Like, there could be overlap or something... People might start to wonder why they remember doing two different things at the same time of day.

80211806.text: That's why he makes sure the memories take place at a specific moment in time, rather than over a period of time.

80211807.text: (If we consider this in conjunction with what we already know, then the question of whose memory this is... seems to have an obvious answer...)

80219901.text: The Abyss Order's on the move... The Ley Lines are all out of whack...

80219902.text: We better hurry back to Vimara Village and see what's going on!
